title: Man. Post. Cap. VII: PLAC meritorie = deserve condemn; judge must not destroy justice
pass_a_gloss: Placeus: to lose justice meritoriously is only to deserve not to be justified by the judge but to be condemned. To deserve that a judge as punishment strip the habit of justice is to deserve that he take away what is not and do what fights a lawgiver's and judge's justice—he is bound rather to conserve justice than destroy it or take it from the endowed, and it does not become him to make those he judges into unjust sinners. Comparing the faithful in grace with Adam in nature is inapt: fallen nature and the state of grace are opposed, not alike. Adam's justice was a natural gift; the justice inhering in us is a supernatural gift.
pass_b_english: PLAC. First, what is it to lose justice meritoriously, if not to deserve not to be justified by the judge, but to be condemned? For to deserve that as punishment the judge take from him the habit of justice is to deserve that the judge take away what is not, and do what seems to fight with the justice of the lawgiver and of the judge. For the judge is rather bound to conserve justice than to destroy it, and to take it from him who is endowed with it. Nor does it become him to make those whom he judges unjust and sinners. That the comparison he institutes between the faithful in the state of grace and Adam in the state of nature is not apt, no one, I think, fails to see. For they are opposed to each other—so far are they from being alike—the state of fallen nature and the state of grace. Adam's justice was a natural gift; the justice inhering in us is a supernatural gift.
source_text: PLAC. Primum quid est amittere justitiam meritorie, nisi mereri non justificari a judice, sed condemnari? Nam mereri, ut pro poena judex ab eo auferat justitiae habitum, est mereri ut judex tollat quod non est, & faciat id quod cum justitia legislatoris & judicis pugnare videtur. Tenetur enim potius judex conservare justitiam, quam destruere, & ab eo qui ea praeditus est, tollere. Nec enim eum decet eos, quos judicat, facere injustos & peccatores. Comparatio quam instituit inter fideles in statu gratiae, & Adamum in statu naturae, quam non sit apposita, nemo, opinor, non videt. Opponuntur enim inter se, tantum abest ut sint similes, status naturae lapsae, & status gratiae. Justitia Adami erat donum naturale, justitia nobis inhaerens est donum supernaturale.

choices.choice: Meritorie = deserve condemn; judge must not destroy justice; nature≠grace
